planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in full sun; Oktoberfest flowers notably earlier than most Miscanthus sinensis selections, so give it a prominent spot where its early-season plumes and strong fall color can be seen before the main maiden-grass display begins.

directions: Oktoberfest is a Walters Gardens introduction selected for its unusually early bloom and intense fall color. Dense, upright-arching clumps of green foliage send up reddish-maroon flower plumes by late summer, well ahead of most other maiden grass cultivars, and the plumes age to a soft silvery tan while the foliage turns deep burgundy-purple with red highlights in autumn. It forms a tidy, well-behaved clump that holds its shape through winter and is useful as a specimen, screen, or back-of-border accent. Cut the whole clump back hard in late winter before new growth emerges.

common_name: Dronning Ingrid Maiden Grass (Queen Ingrid Miscanthus)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in full sun and well-drained soil with room for a dense, upright clump; foliage color intensifies through summer into a vivid red fall display.

directions: Dronning Ingrid (named for a Danish queen) was selected at Overdam Nursery in Denmark and is grown chiefly for its exceptional autumn foliage color. Narrow, upright-arching leaves carry a pale central stripe and develop purple-red tints from early summer, intensifying to a vivid, fiery red by fall. Fox-red flower plumes open above the foliage in late summer and persist as the leaves color up beneath them, giving two overlapping seasons of display from a single clump. Grow in full sun and average, well-drained soil; cut the clump back hard in late winter before new growth emerges.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in full sun; Krater stays more compact than many maiden grass cultivars, making it a good fit for smaller borders where a full-sized Miscanthus would overwhelm the space.

directions: Krater is a German-raised maiden grass selection valued for its comparatively compact size and strong fall color. Narrow, upright-to-arching green leaves turn purple-red in autumn, and slender, arching flower plumes open brick-red in late summer before aging to a silvery grey that persists into winter. Its smaller stature compared to many Miscanthus sinensis cultivars suits it to mid-border placement or smaller gardens where larger selections would be out of scale. Grow in full sun and average to moist, well-drained soil, and cut the clump back hard in late winter.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in full sun; Afrika begins coloring for fall earlier than most Miscanthus sinensis selections, extending the season of foliage interest.

directions: Afrika is grown for unusually early and intense autumn foliage color. Olive-green leaves begin turning orange and red from mid-to-late summer, well ahead of most other maiden grass cultivars, deepening to a rich red through fall. Dark brownish-red flower plumes appear on tall stems above the foliage in late summer and autumn. Grow in full sun and average, well-drained soil; cut the whole clump back hard in late winter before new growth emerges.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in full sun; the upright red flower plumes age to silvery white and are a strong feature through fall and into winter above the colored foliage.

directions: Rotfuchs (German for 'red fox') is a German-bred maiden grass selection prized for the contrast between its colored foliage and persistent winter plumes. Narrow, arching leaves emerge green and shift to orange-brown in autumn, while upright red to dark-red flower plumes open in late summer and gradually age to a silvery white that remains attractive through much of winter. Grow in full sun and average, well-drained soil; cut the clump back hard in late winter before new growth emerges.

common_name: Super Stripe Maiden Grass (Zebra Super Stripe Miscanthus)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in full sun with room for the clump to reach its full height once flower stems extend well above the foliage in early fall.

directions: Super Stripe is a patented zebra-type maiden grass selected for bolder, more consistent horizontal gold banding across the leaf blades than older zebra-grass cultivars such as 'Zebrinus'. The upright, arching clump of banded foliage tops out around four feet, with tawny-bronze flower plumes rising another two to three feet above it in early fall. Grow in full sun and average, well-drained soil; stake-free and self-supporting under normal conditions, it is best sited where the leaf banding can be viewed up close. Cut the clump back hard in late winter before new growth emerges.

common_name: Fire Dragon Maiden Grass (Mystal Series Fire Dragon Miscanthus)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in full sun; Fire Dragon reliably turns vivid orange-red for several weeks beginning in early October, so site it where the fall color display will be visible from indoors or a seating area.

directions: Fire Dragon is part of PlantHaven's Mystal series of maiden grass selections, bred for reliable, vivid autumn foliage color even in cooler climates. Upright, vigorous green foliage turns striking orange-red for about four to five weeks beginning in early October, and silvery-grey, silky flower plumes appear reliably above the clump in late summer. It is more cold-tolerant than many Miscanthus sinensis selections, performing well into zone 4. Grow in full sun and average, well-drained soil, and cut the clump back hard in late winter before new growth emerges.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in full sun; flower plumes open deep maroon-red and are a strong late-summer feature before fading to silver for the winter.

directions: Red Chief is a European-raised maiden grass selection with narrow, apple-green leaves marked by a pale silvery midrib through summer, turning yellow in autumn. Deep maroon-red-pink flower plumes open in late summer and gradually fade to silver, remaining decorative on the plant well into winter. Grow in full sun and average, well-drained soil; cut the clump back hard in late winter before new growth emerges.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in full sun with ample room; Silberturm ('silver tower') is among the tallest maiden grass selections and needs a large-scale setting to be shown to advantage.

directions: Silberturm is one of the tallest Miscanthus sinensis selections in general cultivation, forming a towering column of broad, arching green leaf blades that can reach eight to nine feet. Large, silvery-white flower plumes open high above the foliage in late summer and fall, shimmering in low light. Because of its considerable scale, it is best used as a large specimen, seasonal screen, or back-of-border accent rather than in small gardens. Grow in full sun and average, well-drained soil, and cut the clump back hard in late winter before new growth emerges.

common_name: Gold Fontaene Giant Feather Grass (Golden Oats)

planting.note: Plant in very well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline, lean soil in full sun; like the species, Gold Fontaene requires excellent drainage and dislikes waterlogged soil in winter.

directions: Gold Fontaene is a selection of giant feather grass raised for more intensely golden, long-persisting flower heads than the straight species, and it has received the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit. It forms the same dense, semi-evergreen mound of narrow, arching green leaves as the species, from which numerous tall, transparent flowering stems rise in summer, reaching five to six feet and bearing golden-brown, oat-like spikelets that catch the light. Plant in sharply drained, lean, neutral to alkaline soil in full sun, as for the species, and avoid heavy or waterlogged ground, especially over winter.

common_name: Pixie Giant Feather Grass (Dwarf Golden Oats)

planting.note: Plant in very well-drained, lean, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Pixie is a true dwarf and is well suited to containers and small gardens where full-sized Stipa gigantea would be too large.

directions: Pixie is a compact, dwarf selection of giant feather grass, scaled down for containers and smaller gardens. It forms a dense mound of narrow, tough, semi-evergreen leaves at a fraction of the size of the species, yet still produces the same open, branched panicles of golden, oat-like flowers in summer and autumn. Plant in sharply drained, lean soil in full sun, exactly as for the species; it is slower-growing and far less imposing than full-sized Stipa gigantea but offers a similar luminous, backlit seedhead display at patio scale.

common_name: Wind Dancer Lovegrass (Wind Dancer Elliott's Love Grass)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in well-drained, sandy to loamy soil in full sun in spring; Wind Dancer is reported hardy to zone 6, slightly more cold-tolerant than typical straight-species plants.

directions: Wind Dancer is a Digging Dog Nursery selection of Elliott's lovegrass chosen for its especially fine, glaucous blue-green foliage and abundant, long-lasting flower panicles. The gauzy, airy plumes mature from buff to straw tones over the season, creating an ethereal, translucent haze when backlit. Like the species it tolerates dry, poor soil, heat, and salt exposure, making it useful in containers, mixed borders, coastal gardens, and meadow plantings; it is reported hardy to zone 6. Cut back old foliage in late winter before new growth emerges.

common_name: Algau Silver Spike Grass (Allgau Needle Grass)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in full sun and lean, sharply drained soil; Algau holds a tidier, more strictly upright form than the straight species and resents heavy, wet winter ground.

directions: Algau is an upright-growing selection of silver spike grass (syn. Achnatherum calamagrostis) valued for its long season of soft, drooping, feathery flower panicles, which open silvery and age to golden-brown, persisting from early summer into winter. Unlike the more lax habit of the straight species, Algau holds a strictly upright, vertical clump with gracefully nodding plumes. It prefers lean, well-drained, neutral to alkaline soil in full sun and resents heavy, wet winter conditions, but tolerates considerable drought once established. More cold-hardy than Stipa gigantea, it suits dry gravel gardens, border fronts, and naturalistic plantings.
